subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- August 15, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - August 15, 2026

Development work has been steadily progressing across the AcreetionOS ecosystem, with several key repositories receiving attention this week. The team has been focused on refining the core distribution components and ensuring smooth deployment pipelines. Recent commits show activity in the main ISO build repository and the appstore integration, both critical pieces of the user experience.

The logo assets received a minor update to restore the crisp vector version of logo.webp, reverting a larger redraw that wasn't quite matching the project's visual identity. On the website front, download links are now properly pointing to live GitHub releases, and a new Awesome card has been added to showcase community contributions. These frontend fixes help keep the public-facing materials consistent with the project's brand and messaging.

Infrastructure maintenance continues with deploy key fixes triggering GitLab mirror re-syncs across multiple repositories. The acreetionos-archiso project has been updated to mirror to a valid GitLab project path, which should improve reliability for contributors using the self-hosted instance. These behind-the-scenes adjustments are essential for maintaining the distributed development workflow that the small but dedicated team relies on.

The Acreetion Appstore is seeing feature development momentum, with work on a new settings system, an AUR sidebar toggle, grid view options, and AppImage auto-registration. These additions aim to provide users with more control over their software management experience within the Cinnamon desktop environment. The appstore remains a key area of focus for making AcreetionOS more accessible to new Linux users.

Community discussions have been active around recent developments in the broader Arch Linux ecosystem, including news about prominent developer resignations and security concerns with AUR packages. The team has added a welcome message for first-time contributors in CI workflows, which helps foster a more inclusive environment for new developers. These community engagement efforts reflect the project's commitment to growing its contributor base while staying true to its privacy-focused values.

Recent security incidents in the Linux community have highlighted the importance of repository sovereignty, which aligns closely with AcreetionOS's core philosophy. The project continues to emphasize no telemetry and user control over their system data. These recent events serve as a reminder of why independent, community-driven distributions like AcreetionOS matter in today's computing landscape.

Looking ahead, the development roadmap includes further refinements to the Calamares installer customization and continued work on ISO pipeline infrastructure. Darren's focus on backend systems engineering, including kernel configurations and CI/CD pipelines, remains crucial for maintaining build reliability. The team's two-person approach continues to balance technical excellence with user-friendly design principles.

On the personal development front, the team behind AcreetionOS continues to share their journey through various platforms. Natalie's personal site features deep dives into her experiences and the philosophical foundations of the project, while Darren's GitLab profile showcases his gaming and systems engineering background. This transparency about the people behind the code helps build stronger connections with the community.

As always, users experiencing issues or looking to contribute can find support through the official Discord server or by browsing the project's documentation. The team remains committed to providing a lightweight, privacy-focused Linux distribution that doesn't compromise on usability. Stay tuned for more updates as development continues pushing toward the next milestone release.
